newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac gets agreement for Congo truce.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac gets agreement for Congo truce.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac has obtained agreement for a ceasefire from the warring sides in the Congo, his office said on Monday.
Chirac's spokeswoman said he had received verbal agreement for a ceasefire in telephone conversations with President Pascal Lissouba and his opponent, former president Denis Sassou-Nguesso.

Chirac asked the two adversaries "to decide on a ceasefire as soon as possible and accept the mediation of (Gabon President) Omar Bongo to seek a political solution and he obtained their agreement in principle," spokeswoman Catherine Colonna told reporters.
She said Chirac told the two men that resorting to arms was unacceptable and "there can be no military solution to a political problem."
Chirac earlier spoke to Bongo, she said.
Chirac's intervention came as France, the former colonial power, sent more troops to embattled Brazzaville, bringing the number of French troops there to 1,200.
